# LS-12 Sanitary Lift Station: Control Narrative (Draft A)

**Status:** Draft for review. Not for construction.
**Date:** 2026-10-18
**Basis:** Operations request for LS-12. The instrument index, P&ID, alarm database and C&E chart were not supplied. Tags marked *TBC* are placeholders.

Values marked **TBD** or **ASSUMED** are not in the request. Section 10 lists them as open items.

---

## 1. Purpose and boundaries

| Item | Description |
|---|---|
| Function | LS-12 lifts sewage from the wet well to the downstream force main. It keeps the wet well level below the overflow elevation. |
| Priority | Prevent overflow to the creek. This goal outranks pump wear and energy use. |
| Upstream | Gravity inlet sewer. Inflow is not measured or controlled. |
| Downstream | Force main (tag *TBC*). |
| Control system | Station PLC. It reports to central SCADA over licensed radio. |
| Power | Utility feed and standby generator, selected by the automatic transfer switch (ATS-12, *TBC*). |
| Out of scope | Alarm text and priorities (alarm database). Any SIS function (see 6.3). Tuning of the VFD (VFD commissioning record). |

---

## 2. Equipment and tags

The instrument index is the master list. This section only names the tags used in this document.

| Tag | Description | Note |
|---|---|---|
| LIT-121 | Submersible level transmitter, 0-3.0 m | Primary level signal |
| LSL-121 | Low level float switch | Backup |
| LSHH-121 | High-high level float switch | Backup |
| P-121, P-122 | Submersible pumps, each 100% duty | |
| VFD-121, VFD-122 | Pump drives (*TBC*) | |
| HS-121, HS-122 | Hand-Off-Auto switches at the MCC (*TBC*) | |
| ATS-12 | Automatic transfer switch (*TBC*) | |

---

---

## 4. Station modes and pump states (ISA-106)

### 4.1 Station states (state-based control)

| State | Entry permissive | Behavior | Automation level |
|---|---|---|---|
| ST-1 Normal | LIT-121 is good. No restart hold. LSHH-121 is clear. | Lead/lag control by LIT-121 (section 5). | Automatic |
| ST-2 Overflow Protection | LSHH-121 is active, **or** LIT-121 is at or above SP-015. | Start every available pump in Auto at SP-021. | Automatic |
| ST-3 Float Backup | LIT-121 is bad (see 8). | Control by LSL-121 and LSHH-121 only. | Automatic |
| ST-4 Restart Hold | Power was restored, or the PLC restarted. | Pumps stay stopped until the stagger delays end. | Automatic |

### 4.2 Station transitions

| From | To | Initiator | Condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| ST-4 | ST-1 | Auto | Stagger delays are complete and LIT-121 is good. |
| ST-4 | ST-3 | Auto | Stagger delays are complete and LIT-121 is bad. |
| ST-4 | ST-2 | Auto | LSHH-121 is active. Skip the stagger delay (FR-LS12-031). |
| ST-1 | ST-2 | Auto | Entry permissive of ST-2 is true. |
| ST-1 | ST-3 | Auto | LIT-121 becomes bad. |
| ST-2 | ST-1 | Auto | LSHH-121 is clear, LIT-121 is good, and LIT-121 is at or below SP-011. |
| ST-2 | ST-3 | Auto | LIT-121 is bad and LSHH-121 is clear. |
| ST-3 | ST-1 | Auto | LIT-121 is good for the time in SP-034. |
| ST-3 | ST-2 | Auto | LSHH-121 is active. |
| Any | ST-4 | Auto | PLC restart or loss of the pump power bus. |

### 4.3 Pump states (equipment module P-121, P-122)

| State | Entry permissive | Allowed exits | Initiator |
|---|---|---|---|
| Out of Service | HS is not in Auto. | Available | Operator, by HS |
| Available | HS in Auto. No fault. LSL-121 is clear of the low-level condition. SP-031 elapsed. | Starting, Out of Service, Faulted | Auto |
| Starting | Start call from the station. | Running, Faulted | Auto |
| Running | VFD run feedback is true. | Stopping, Faulted, Out of Service | Auto |
| Stopping | Stop call, or low-level condition. | Available, Faulted | Auto |
| Faulted | VFD fault, start or stop proof failure, or motor protection trip. | Available | Operator reset, after the cause is cleared |

The Hand position runs the pump outside the PLC (see 9). The Hand position is a special case of Out of Service.

---

## 5. Regulatory and level control

### 5.1 Level control loop

| Item | Definition |
|---|---|
| PV | LIT-121 level, filtered |
| Output | VFD-121 and VFD-122 speed references, and run commands |
| Action | Speed rises as level rises |
| Mode | Auto only. There is no operator speed setpoint in Auto. |
| Cascade or override | None. ST-2 overrides the lead/lag logic. |

### 5.2 Requirements, ST-1 Normal

| ID | Requirement | Test method |
|---|---|---|
| FR-LS12-001 | The PLC shall assign one available pump as lead and the other as lag. | FAT: simulate LIT-121. Check lead and lag tags. |
| FR-LS12-002 | The PLC shall start the lead pump when LIT-121 rises to SP-012. | FAT: ramp LIT-121 up. Record the start level. |
| FR-LS12-003 | The PLC shall set the lead speed reference to SP-020 at SP-012. | FAT: read the speed reference at SP-012. |
| FR-LS12-004 | The PLC shall raise the lead speed reference linearly from SP-020 at SP-012 to SP-021 at SP-013. | FAT: record the reference at four levels between SP-012 and SP-013. |
| FR-LS12-005 | The PLC shall hold the lead speed reference at SP-021 for all levels above SP-013. | FAT: set LIT-121 above SP-013. Read the reference. |
| FR-LS12-006 | While the lead pump runs, the PLC shall use the same level-to-speed curve when level falls. It shall hold SP-020 below SP-012. | FAT: ramp LIT-121 down. Read the reference. |
| FR-LS12-007 | The PLC shall start the lag pump when LIT-121 is at or above SP-013 for the time in SP-033. | FAT: hold LIT-121 above SP-013. Record the delay. |
| FR-LS12-008 | The PLC shall run the lag pump at SP-022. | FAT: read the lag speed reference. |
| FR-LS12-009 | The PLC shall stop the lag pump when LIT-121 falls to SP-023. | FAT: ramp LIT-121 down. Record the stop level. |
| FR-LS12-010 | The PLC shall stop the lead pump when LIT-121 falls to SP-011. | FAT: ramp LIT-121 down. Record the stop level. |
| FR-LS12-011 | After all pumps stop, the PLC shall swap the lead and lag assignment. | FAT: run three cycles. Check that the lead pump changes each cycle. |
| FR-LS12-012 | If only one pump is Available, the PLC shall assign it as lead and shall not swap. | FAT: put one HS in Off. Run one cycle. |
| FR-LS12-013 | If the lead pump faults while running, the PLC shall start the lag pump at once. It shall not wait for SP-013. | FAT: trip VFD-121 while it is lead. Check that P-122 starts. |
| FR-LS12-014 | The PLC shall enforce SP-030, SP-031 and SP-032 on each pump. | FAT: cycle the level. Check the holds. |
| FR-LS12-015 | The PLC shall not enforce SP-031 or SP-032 when LIT-121 is at or above SP-014. | FAT: set level high. Check that a pump starts. |
| FR-LS12-016 | The PLC shall ramp VFD speed with the time in SP-024. | FAT: step the reference. Time the ramp. |

FR-LS12-015 gives overflow prevention priority over the pump wear limits. Section 10 lists this for approval.

### 5.3 Requirements, ST-2 Overflow Protection

| ID | Requirement | Test method |
|---|---|---|
| FR-LS12-020 | The PLC shall enter ST-2 when LSHH-121 is active, even if LIT-121 reads a lower level. | FAT: close the LSHH-121 contact with LIT-121 low. |
| FR-LS12-021 | In ST-2 the PLC shall start every Available pump at SP-021. It shall ignore SP-031, SP-032 and SP-033. | FAT: as FR-LS12-020. Check both pumps. |
| FR-LS12-022 | In ST-2 the PLC shall run the pumps until LIT-121 is at or below SP-011, or LSL-121 indicates low level. | FAT: lower the level. Record the stop level. |
| FR-LS12-023 | The PLC shall start the pumps in ST-2 with a stagger of at most the time in SP-063 between starts (generator only). | FAT: repeat on generator power. |

---

## 6. Interlocks, permissives and protection

### 6.1 Interlocks

The cause-and-effect chart CE-LS12 (to be issued) is the master. This narrative does not restate its logic.

| ID | Requirement | Reference | Test method |
|---|---|---|---|
| FR-LS12-040 | The PLC shall implement all interlocks in CE-LS12. | CE-LS12 | FAT: run every row of CE-LS12. |
| FR-LS12-041 | A low-level condition on LSL-121 shall stop both pumps in Auto. | CE-LS12 | FAT: open LSL-121 with pumps running. |
| FR-LS12-042 | A low-level condition on LSL-121 shall override a start call from LIT-121, unless ST-2 applies and LSHH-121 is active. | CE-LS12 | FAT: set LIT-121 high and LSL-121 low. |

### 6.2 Alarms

The alarm database ALM-LS12 (to be issued) lists the alarm text, priority and response. The alarm database needs at least these alarm conditions:

| Condition | Source | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| High level | LIT-121 at SP-014 | ALM-LS12 |
| High-high level | LSHH-121 | ALM-LS12 |
| Low level | LSL-121 | ALM-LS12 |
| LIT-121 bad | SP-040, SP-041 | ALM-LS12 |
| LIT/float deviation | SP-042, SP-043 | ALM-LS12 |
| Pump fault, start fail, stop fail | P-121, P-122 | ALM-LS12 |
| Pump not in Auto | HS-121, HS-122 | ALM-LS12 |
| Generator running | ATS-12 | ALM-LS12 |
| SCADA comms loss | SP-050 | ALM-LS12 |
| Power failure | ATS-12 | ALM-LS12 |

### 6.3 Safety instrumented functions

This document does not specify any SIS function. LSHH-121 is the last layer before an overflow that is a permit violation. Open item OI-01 decides whether this function needs a risk assessment under IEC 61511. If it does, the SRS owns the function and this narrative shall reference it.

---

## 7. Sequences (sequence-based control)

### 7.1 SQ-1 Pump start (P-121 or P-122)

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Check the pump Available permissives. | All are true. | Immediate | End the sequence. Select the other pump. |
| 2 | Send the speed reference at the value for the current duty. | Reference written. | Immediate | None |
| 3 | Send the VFD run command. | VFD run feedback is true. | SP-071 | Stop the command. Set the pump to Faulted. Raise start-fail alarm. Call the other pump. |
| 4 | Release the speed reference to the level curve (lead) or SP-022 (lag). | Pump state is Running. | Immediate | None |

### 7.2 SQ-2 Pump stop

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Remove the run command. | VFD run feedback is false. | SP-072 | Set the pump to Faulted. Raise stop-fail alarm. |
| 2 | Start the SP-031 timer. | Timer complete. | SP-031 | None |
| 3 | Set the pump to Available. | State is Available. | Immediate | None |

SQ-2 uses a stop by command and not a ramp, because the VFD ramps down at SP-024.

### 7.3 SQ-3 Restart after power loss

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Set ST-4. Hold all run commands off. | PLC runs and the pump power bus is live. | None | Remain in ST-4. |
| 2 | Wait for SP-063 after the ATS change. | Timer complete. | SP-063 | None |
| 3 | Start the P-121 delay SP-060. | Timer complete. | SP-060 | None |
| 4 | Start the P-122 delay SP-061. | Timer complete. | SP-061 | None |
| 5 | Leave ST-4 by the table in 4.2. | Station state is set. | Immediate | None |

The PLC shall start a pump after its delay only if the level logic calls for it.

---

## 8. Abnormal handling

| ID | Event | Required response | Test method |
|---|---|---|---|
| FR-LS12-030 | LIT-121 signal is outside SP-040 or SP-041. | Set LIT-121 bad. Enter ST-3. Raise the alarm. | FAT: force the loop current out of range. |
| FR-LS12-031 | LSHH-121 active in any state, including ST-4. | Enter ST-2. Do not wait for stagger delays. | FAT: close LSHH-121 during restart. |
| FR-LS12-032 | In ST-3, LSHH-121 becomes active. | Start every Available pump at SP-021. Run until LSL-121 indicates low level. | FAT: close LSHH-121 with LIT-121 bad. |
| FR-LS12-033 | LIT-121 and the floats disagree for SP-043 by more than SP-042. | Raise the deviation alarm. Keep LIT-121 in control. | FAT: hold LSHH-121 active with LIT-121 low. |
| FR-LS12-034 | SCADA heartbeat is lost for SP-050. | Raise the comms alarm. Keep all control in the PLC. | FAT: disconnect the radio. |
| FR-LS12-035 | SCADA sends a command while comms are restored. | The PLC shall accept only the commands in section 9. | FAT: send a pump start from SCADA. Check rejection. |
| FR-LS12-036 | Utility power fails. | ATS-12 transfers to the generator. The PLC enters ST-4 and runs SQ-3. | SAT: open the utility breaker. |
| FR-LS12-037 | On generator power. | Run no more than SP-062 pumps, except in ST-2 (see 10, OI-05). | SAT: raise level on generator. |
| FR-LS12-038 | PLC restarts. | The PLC enters ST-4. The lead assignment returns to the last saved value. | FAT: cycle PLC power. |
| FR-LS12-039 | VFD, motor or seal fault. | Set the pump to Faulted. Start the other pump if called. Latch until operator reset. | FAT: trip each fault input. |

**Fail positions.** All pump outputs are de-energized on loss of the PLC output. The pumps stop. LSL-121 and LSHH-121 contacts shall be wired fail-safe, so that a broken wire reads as the alarm condition. The wiring diagram shall show the contact type.

**Loss of PLC.** No pump runs under Auto if the PLC is down. This is a gap in overflow protection (see OI-02).

---

## 9. Operator interface

### 9.1 Local, at the MCC

| ID | Requirement | Test method |
|---|---|---|
| FR-LS12-050 | In Hand, the pump runs from the MCC at SP-070. The PLC cannot stop it. | FAT: set HS to Hand. Check run and speed. |
| FR-LS12-051 | In Off, the pump does not run. | FAT: set HS to Off. |
| FR-LS12-052 | In Auto, the PLC controls the pump. | FAT: set HS to Auto. Check SQ-1. |
| FR-LS12-053 | The PLC shall read each HS position and report it to SCADA. | FAT: change HS. Check the SCADA tag. |
| FR-LS12-054 | Whether Hand honors LSL-121 is open (OI-03). | See OI-03. |

### 9.2 SCADA

| ID | Requirement | Test method |
|---|---|---|
| FR-LS12-060 | SCADA shall show LIT-121 level, LSL-121, LSHH-121, pump state, pump speed, HS position, station state, and power source. | FAT: compare each point with the PLC. |
| FR-LS12-061 | SCADA shall show the level setpoints from section 3 as read-only. | FAT: check the display. |
| FR-LS12-062 | SCADA shall show pump run time and start count. | FAT: run a cycle. Check the counters. |
| FR-LS12-063 | SCADA shall allow the operator to reset a Faulted pump. | FAT: send a reset. |
| FR-LS12-064 | SCADA shall allow the operator to select a fixed lead pump instead of alternation. | FAT: select P-122. Run two cycles. |
| FR-LS12-065 | SCADA shall not start or stop a pump. | FAT: attempt a start. |
| FR-LS12-066 | Setpoint changes shall need a security level (OI-04). | FAT: attempt a change at a low level. |

## 11. Review notes

These points need a decision before the integrator starts. The first three are in the open items above.

1. **The margin to overflow is small.** LSHH-121 is at 2.6 m and the overflow is at 2.8 m. The high level alarm is at 2.3 m. The operator has little time to respond. See OI-01, OI-02 and OI-11.
2. **The lag pump has no defined stop level or speed.** I assumed that the lag stops with the lead and runs at maximum speed. See OI-06.
3. **The floats have no stated function.** I assigned LSL-121 as a pump protection stop. I assigned LSHH-121 as a start of every available pump, independent of LIT-121. Confirm both.

**Checks status**

| Check | Status |
|---|---|
| No setpoints in prose | Done. Values are only in section 3. |
| Requirement IDs and test methods | Done for FR-LS12-001 to 066. |
| States with permissives and exits | Done in 4.1 to 4.3. |
| Sequence steps with timeout and failure response | Done. Timeout values are TBD in the SP list. |
| Abnormal handling | Done in section 8. |
| Alarms and interlocks referenced | Done. CE-LS12 and ALM-LS12 are not yet issued. |
| SIS referenced | Done. See OI-01. |
| Open items with owner and date | Done. |
| STE pass | Done for the main text. Do a full STE edit after the open items close. |

I have not yet checked the details of the STE edit against the ASD-STE100 dictionary. The next step after the open items close is a full edit pass and a FAT procedure that follows the test-method column.
